userVisible: A module can check itself on every start: it creates its database, applies its migrations and reports that everything is in order.
A bot can ask a module to store something and later read back everything it stored, and gets the same answer for the same question.
Every module answers the same way: one JSON answer per command, fixed exit codes, repeatable output, no access to the bot's private data, and analysis that never changes data.
A module written in Python is held to exactly the same rules as one written in TypeScript, and each language's tests accept the other's module.
check: npm run --silent build:python && npm run --silent contract:python

userVisible: A bot can install a module on every start: the download is checked against its published checksum, installing twice changes nothing, and a damaged download never replaces a working module.

A module that needs a large native package can have it installed only when the person asks: the package list is checked against its published checksum, every package is checked against its pinned hash, a failed or interrupted install never leaves a half-built runtime in place, and installing twice changes nothing. Without it the module still answers selfcheck and says in plain words what is missing.

userVisible: A bot keeps every pinned module in place with one command: it installs what is missing, replaces what was removed or altered, upgrades when a pin moves, runs each selfcheck and says in plain words what happened. A newer template release is only reported: nothing from it is downloaded, installed or run.

Under instructions version 6 or later the daily selfcheck can upgrade the installer only when the authenticated service checksum, the public release checksum and the downloaded bytes agree. Downgrades are refused, old files are kept, and the link changes only after verification.

An instructions proposal merges the published update with local changes, lists the local changes kept, shows both sides of conflicts or an unknown base, and states which permissions can be compared. The owner alone pastes it; neither input file is changed.

Daily update checks retain service announcements and announce tool changes once. The daily snapshot starts active, waits silently for monitoring readiness, builds its review Page once a week with high priority items before low, and sends reports only with platform-confirmed pre-approval; feedback still needs approval for each call.

A bot whose instructions come from an earlier template is told so, with the newer text, the lines that differ, and in plain words which permissions the newer text would add or take away. A careful copy by hand that differs only in whitespace is still recognised. A text the owner wrote is recognised as theirs and left alone. When the installer is itself behind a newer template, the bot says so and recommends updating the template first. Only the owner ever changes a bot's instructions, and the skills keep working with the earlier ones.

A bot whose routine still runs a prompt from an earlier template is told so, with the newer prompt. A published prompt that was stored with its destination line added is still recognised. A missing routine and a prompt the owner changed are told apart, and nothing is changed until the owner asks.

A bot finds its connection to the Ambitious monitoring service by the tools the connector offers and, where its instructions allow, by the identity the service answers with. A connector that only has the right name is left alone, and the bot says how many connectors had their tools read and which did not.

A bot writes a shared skill from a file the installer wrote and checks what was stored against the checksum the installer printed, so a skill is never retyped and never taken from anywhere but the pinned installer.

A bot reads the long procedures and field tables from the pinned installer when it needs them, so its skills stay short. The checksum pin and the fetch lines stay in the installer skill itself, and every skill says to fetch the pinned installer first when a guide cannot be read.

The owner can ask the bot to find ready-made bots for the business in the Ambitious catalog. Under instructions version 7 the bot shows the exact description before it is sent, proposes the bots in a Page and creates one only after the owner approves; under older instructions it calls no factory tool and proposes the version 7 text.
check: node --test --test-name-pattern='version 7|hard rules stay|no skill and no routine requires' template/test/check.test.mjs && node --test --test-name-pattern='template 0.3.1' template/test/e2e.test.mjs

userVisible: The bot template stays small enough to be typed into the platform: every skill and both routine prompts are held to one size budget, a conservative one and not a measured platform limit, and a release over it cannot be built.

The snapshot routine keeps daily evidence locally and builds the review Page and any new report when due: on its first run and after at least 7 full days since the last Page. Pending report review and delivery continue on other days. It stays silent unless something changed or needs the owner, including a module failure or new high-priority finding.

Anyone may ask a bot for an upgrade that writes its skills only when the bot's own instructions are a published text that says so; under every other text only the owner may. The request itself supplies nothing: no pin, no address and no skill text.
check: node --test --test-name-pattern='asked for by anyone|shared skill' packages/kit/test/sync.test.ts

userVisible: A stray code comment is refused with a message that says what to do instead.
Pure logic that reaches for the database is refused with a message that says where the code belongs.
A new module repository can take the kit from the release files alone and pass every check from its first commit.
Anyone can read and contribute to this repository: nothing in it points at a private plan or at one person's machine.
Every model of how the software behaves passes the model checker, and every deliberately broken copy is caught breaking the rule it was written to break.
